transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the safety review for the opening number. I want to make sure we're all aligned before I sign off on the final stunt plan. I've got the current draft in front of me — single-point harness, 2-meter performer clearance, flame burst at the end of the descent, and a Thursday rehearsal from 3:00 to 5:00 PM. Spectators are currently placed 3 meters from the stage edge with one EMT assigned to the performance area. I need rigging, insurance, talent, and fire-safety leads to confirm any conditions that must be reflected before I approve this plan. Who wants to go first?

transcript.text: Maya, I need to flag two rigging conditions before you sign off. I completed my review of the installed points after yesterday's load test, and my findings require a dual-point harness — not the single-point harness currently in the draft — and exactly 3 meters of unobstructed performer clearance, not the 2 meters currently listed. The revised rigging sheet hasn't been circulated yet, so the draft you're looking at doesn't reflect these requirements.

transcript.text: Maya, I need to flag a critical insurance condition before you sign off. I confirmed with our insurer this morning — the policy explicitly excludes coverage for an open-flame burst effect. However, a cold-spark unit from the approved vendor IS covered under the policy. I received the endorsement email this morning but haven't yet attached it to the production file, so the current draft still references a flame burst, which would leave us uninsured for that effect. We need to either switch to the approved cold-spark unit or resolve the coverage gap before I can confirm this plan.
